body:
Marcus Fields: Owen, Rina — thanks for the call. Elena's here from product. We wanted to work through the Zendesk and Twilio integration questions from the last email thread. That was a long thread.

Owen Trask: It was. And I'll be straight with you — the fact that we're two months into implementation and still working through these blockers is a concern. If we can't resolve this today or in the next week, I'm going to have to escalate internally about whether we continue.

Elena Sokolova: We hear you and we want to get this unblocked. Rina, can you walk us through where you're stuck?

Rina Patel: Sure. Two main issues. First, Twilio. We're on Twilio Flex, not standard Twilio Voice. Your docs assume the standard Voice product. Your webhook signature validation fails against Flex's proxy layer. We have to disable signature validation, which our security team won't accept in production.

Marcus Fields: Yeah, we've hit that before. There's a Flex-specific integration path but it's not documented publicly. I can send you the doc after this call — the short version is you configure a Flex plugin that proxies our webhooks with the correct signature.

Rina Patel: A Flex plugin. Okay. Do you have any customers running that in production today?

Marcus Fields: Two. I can get you a reference call with one of them if it helps.

Owen Trask: That would help.

Rina Patel: Second issue. Zendesk. Your connector reads tickets fine, but when the bot creates a follow-up ticket it doesn't populate our custom fields for product_area and customer_segment. Those are required fields on our side, so every bot-created ticket fails validation and lands in an error queue.

Elena Sokolova: Rina, that's a known gap. Custom field mapping on ticket creation is in our next release, targeting March fifteenth. Until then the workaround is a Zendesk automation on your side that sets those fields to a default value if empty.

Owen Trask: That's not a workaround, that's a hack. We'd have every bot-created ticket showing up with a default product_area, which pollutes our reporting.

Elena Sokolova: I understand. What if we prioritized the custom field mapping ahead of the March release and got it to you in a private build by end of February?

Owen Trask: End of February would be workable. Can you commit to that in writing?

Elena Sokolova: I need to check with my engineering lead but I'm pretty confident. I'll send an email by tomorrow with a firm date.

Owen Trask: Alright. Here's my concern. We signed in October. It's now February. We have not gone live. Our commercial team is asking when we'll see the ROI we sold internally. If we don't have Twilio Flex working and Zendesk custom fields resolved by end of Feb, we're going to look at Bland AI. They reached out last week and their Twilio Flex support is documented.

Marcus Fields: Owen, I hear you. Let me commit to specifics. Twilio Flex plugin doc in your inbox today. Reference call scheduled by end of week. Zendesk custom field mapping in private build by February twenty-eighth. And I'll be on-site with your team the week of the twenty-third for hands-on implementation help.

Owen Trask: On-site would be appreciated. We're in Boston.

Marcus Fields: I'll book flights tonight.

Rina Patel: If Marcus is on-site we can knock out the Flex plugin and the intent tuning at the same time.

Owen Trask: Alright. I'll hold off on escalating for two weeks. If by February twenty-third we don't have Zendesk fixed and Twilio working, we need to have a different conversation.

Elena Sokolova: Understood. We'll deliver.

Rina Patel: One more small thing. Our staging environment doesn't have production data volume. When we do load testing in staging we don't hit the same latency patterns. Any recommendation?

Marcus Fields: We can spin up a production-mirror environment for a week for testing. It's a paid service normally but I'll comp it given the situation.

Rina Patel: Perfect.

Owen Trask: I want to be clear about one more thing. When I say Bland AI reached out — they didn't just email. They offered a full migration package including engineering support. So the switching cost isn't as high as it used to be.

Elena Sokolova: Noted. We take that seriously.

Owen Trask: One question on the roadmap — where does voice_agent_v2 stand? We signed for v1 originally.

Elena Sokolova: V2 is GA. Once your v1 implementation is stable we can migrate you to v2 at no additional cost — it's included in your existing contract. V2 has better handling of interruptions and improved latency, so it's worth the migration.

Owen Trask: When would that migration happen?

Elena Sokolova: I'd recommend after you're stable on v1 in production, probably Q2. It's a two-week project.

Owen Trask: Okay. Let's talk about it once we're live.

Marcus Fields: Thank you, Owen. I know this has been rough. We'll turn it around.

Rina Patel: Talk soon.

Owen Trask: Marcus, one last thing — send me the reference customer names for the Twilio Flex integration by end of day tomorrow.

Marcus Fields: Will do.

Owen Trask: And Elena, I want the private-build ETA in writing by Wednesday.

Elena Sokolova: You'll have it by Tuesday.

Owen Trask: Even better.

Rina Patel: What time zone is Marcus flying in from?

Marcus Fields: Pacific. I'll adjust to Boston hours while I'm there.

Rina Patel: Cool. I'll book the conference room.

Owen Trask: Alright, we good?

Marcus Fields: We're good.

Owen Trask: Talk soon.
